capabilities.name: Company settings and preferences
capabilities.purpose: Explain and control the fiscal, numbering, currency, class, department, and inventory settings that shape all later records.
capabilities.tierRationale: Transactions and reports cannot be interpreted safely without their governing company preferences.

applicability.notes: Preferences and CompanyInfo are documented company-setting entities. Connected-company values and the field-level write policy still require read-only observation.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Per-field API Explorer review plus read-only Preferences observation and manual QBO settings comparison.
limitations: General documentation does not prove that every preference is writable in Canada or by the current app.

capabilities.name: Chart of accounts
capabilities.purpose: Provide the deliberate account structure needed for believable transactions and financial statements.
capabilities.tierRationale: The chart of accounts is the accounting spine for every lifecycle and critical financial report.

applicability.notes: Account is a documented core list resource. Canada subtype and closed-books constraints remain fixture and observation work.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Review the Account API operations and subtype rules, then compare the proposed blueprint against a read-only company inventory.
limitations: List records are deactivated through update rather than hard-deleted.
No business-specific chart of accounts is implemented.

capabilities.name: Customers and customer hierarchy
capabilities.purpose: Represent recognizable customer segments, terms, provinces, sub-customers, contacts, and payment behaviour.
capabilities.tierRationale: Receivables, sales analysis, projects, and manual support reproduction depend on coherent customers.

applicability.notes: Customer is a documented core list resource; the flagship hierarchy and Canadian tax/contact variants remain dataset work.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Per-operation API Explorer review, deterministic fixture review, then paginated sandbox read observation.
limitations: List records are deactivated through update rather than hard-deleted.
Current seeding creates generic names and does not model stable customer behaviour.

capabilities.name: Vendors and terms
capabilities.purpose: Represent supplier segments, contacts, payment terms, tax details, and purchasing behaviour.
capabilities.tierRationale: Payables and purchasing reports require coherent vendors and terms.

applicability.notes: Vendor is a documented core list resource; Canadian tax identifiers and realistic segments remain dataset work.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Per-operation API Explorer review, fixture review, then paginated sandbox read observation.
limitations: List records are deactivated through update rather than hard-deleted.
Current seeding creates generic vendors without persistent behavioural segments.

capabilities.name: Products, services, bundles, and inventory
capabilities.purpose: Exercise service, non-inventory, inventory, category, bundle, quantity, valuation, and purchasing behaviour.
capabilities.tierRationale: The approved business shape and inventory reports require items with correct account relationships and lifecycle effects.

applicability.notes: Inventory is product/preference dependent; the official guide documents item types and inventory behaviour but the connected preference is not yet observed.

preferences: Quantity on hand enabled for inventory

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Official guide and API Explorer review, then read-only Preferences observation and sandbox lifecycle/accounting fixtures.
limitations: Current app creates service items only; no coherent inventory lifecycle exists.

capabilities.name: Sales and receivables lifecycle
capabilities.purpose: Create linked estimates, invoices, sales receipts, payments, credits, refunds, deposits, and realistic open states.
capabilities.tierRationale: Receivables are a central business lifecycle and feed multiple critical reports.

applicability.notes: Invoices, payments, estimates, credit memos, sales receipts, refunds, and related links are documented resources; Canadian tax fixtures remain required.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Entity-by-entity operation/link review, deterministic accounting fixtures, sandbox idempotency tests, and report assertions.
limitations: Current generation covers only narrow randomized AR chains and is not resumable.

Exact create/update operation sections are not recorded from the current per-entity references and remain unknown for all seven entities. Invoice has direct void documentation, while webhook Void events for SalesReceipt, Payment, CreditMemo, and RefundReceipt do not establish an invokable API operation.
The draft entity matrix is maintained in entity-operation-matrix.v1.json; its 18 unknown AR operations and all sandbox mutation evidence remain release-blocking.

capabilities.name: Purchases and payables lifecycle
capabilities.purpose: Create linked purchase orders where supported, bills, expenses, payments, vendor credits, and realistic open states.
capabilities.tierRationale: Payables are a central business lifecycle and feed cash, expense, and liability reporting.

applicability.notes: Bill, BillPayment, Purchase, PurchaseOrder, and VendorCredit are documented transaction resources; Canadian tax fixtures remain required.

preferences: Bills and purchase orders if applicable

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Entity-by-entity operation/link review, deterministic accounting fixtures, sandbox idempotency tests, and report assertions.
limitations: Current generation covers only narrow randomized AP chains and does not model a durable purchasing narrative.

Exact create/update operation sections are not recorded from the current per-entity references and remain unknown for all five entities. Webhook Void events for Purchase and BillPayment do not establish invokable API void operations; both remain unknown.
The draft matrix records 12 unknown AP operations, including the historical Phase 0 PurchaseOrder create failure. No new write path is authorized.

capabilities.name: Banking, cash movement, and cleared state
capabilities.purpose: Represent bank and credit-card accounts, deposits, transfers, purchases, statement periods, and cleared/uncleared activity.
capabilities.tierRationale: Cash flow, balance sheet, close, and reconciliation cannot be credible without explainable bank activity.

applicability.notes: Deposit, Transfer, Purchase, Payment, and account-register data cover the accounting side. Bank-feed matching and official reconciliation remain separate product workflows.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Official entity review, manual product review, sandbox accounting fixtures, and manual reconciliation evidence.
limitations: No bank-feed import or official reconciliation automation is assumed.

capabilities.name: Canadian sales and purchase tax
capabilities.purpose: Represent internally consistent GST, HST, PST, exempt, zero-rated, and out-of-scope treatment across provinces.
capabilities.tierRationale: Canadian tax treatment changes transactions, balances, close work, and critical support/report scenarios.

applicability.notes: The Canada product supports sales-tax setup, transaction tax, liability reports, return preparation, and payment recording. Filing remains external to QBO.

entitlements: Restricted Sales Tax API scope if justified

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Current official non-US/Canada documentation review, Canada sandbox observations, reviewed tax fixtures, and report assertions.
limitations: Restricted Sales Tax API entitlement has not been observed for this app.
Tax correctness and filing behaviour require authoritative Canada-specific fixtures and accounting review.
Canadian returns are filed with the tax agency outside QBO; the product records filing and payment state.

capabilities.name: Projects and project-linked activity
capabilities.purpose: Represent project customers, project estimates, sales, purchases, time/cost, and profitability where entitled.
capabilities.tierRationale: A service/project line is part of the approved flagship business and must have honest product/API coverage.

applicability.notes: Official documentation says Projects and Project API support Advanced, but API access also requires a paid Intuit partner tier, restricted scope, and Projects enabled in company preferences.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Verify current app partner tier and scopes without printing credentials, read ProjectsEnabled, then use separately approved sandbox fixtures.
limitations: Product entitlement alone does not grant the app access to the premium Project API.

capabilities.name: Journal entries and period close
capabilities.purpose: Represent reviewed accruals, deferrals, depreciation, payroll summaries, corrections, retained earnings, and closed-period rules.
capabilities.tierRationale: A continual company and meaningful financial statements require recurring month-end accounting.

applicability.notes: JournalEntry and Preferences are documented. Golden Canadian accounting fixtures and closed-period behaviour remain required before writes.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: API Explorer review, golden debit/credit fixtures, closed-period contract tests, and sandbox report assertions.
limitations: The current random journal generation is not a reviewed close lifecycle.

capabilities.name: Bank and credit-card reconciliation
capabilities.purpose: Track statement periods, cleared activity, differences, adjustments, reviewer evidence, and official QBO confirmation honestly.
capabilities.tierRationale: Reconciliation is essential to a believable continual company even if the official action is UI-only.

applicability.notes: The Canada product documents statement-based reconciliation, zero-difference completion, history, and a static reconciliation report.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Official product/API review followed by a manual QBO procedure and evidence design; do not infer official completion from transaction flags.
limitations: No reconciliation entity or report endpoint appears in the reviewed official Accounting API entity/report indexes as of the verification date; re-check those indexes when Intuit changes them.
The app may prepare statement fixtures and evidence but must not claim to complete the official QBO reconciliation action.

capabilities.name: Budgets and comparisons
capabilities.purpose: Provide business targets that make management and budget-versus-actual reports meaningful.
capabilities.tierRationale: Budgets broaden Advanced and management-report coverage after the accounting spine is stable.

applicability.notes: The Canada product supports profit-and-loss and balance-sheet budgets. The current REST API Explorer exposes Budget for read/query; write support is still unverified.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Current product and API documentation review, manual UI inventory, then fixture/report validation.
limitations: General budget write operations are not established by the current official-source pass; keep create/update/delete manual until API Explorer review is recorded.
The separate premium Project Budget API is US-only for the documented QBO Advanced use case and is not a Canada substitute.

capabilities.name: Classes, locations/departments, and other dimensions
capabilities.purpose: Create enough dimension variation for operational analysis, filtering, and Advanced feature coverage.
capabilities.tierRationale: Dimensions materially broaden reports but depend on the core accounts, entities, and transactions.

applicability.notes: Official Preferences fields document class and department tracking flags; connected-company settings remain unobserved.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Preferences and entity API review, read-only setting observation, then sandbox dimension/report fixtures.
limitations: Settings availability does not prove representative dimensional data exists.
Premium Dimensions API entitlement has not been observed for this app.

capabilities.name: QBO company users and roles
capabilities.purpose: Track expected company users, custom roles, access boundaries, verification dates, evidence, and manual procedures.
capabilities.tierRationale: Users and roles are P0 coverage but must not be conflated with Test Data Lab authorization.

applicability.notes: The Canada Advanced product documents users, standard roles, custom roles, invitations, access changes, and deletion.

entitlements: Appropriate QBO company administrator authority for manual verification

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Current official product and API review plus manual QBO user/role inventory; never infer QBO role from app role.
limitations: No company-user administration entity appears in the reviewed official Accounting API index as of the verification date; re-check on documentation changes.
Application roles are not evidence of QBO company roles.
Coverage must be maintained as a redacted manual inventory and never by storing invitations or credentials.

capabilities.name: Reports API and evidence normalization
capabilities.purpose: Retrieve supported reports, preserve parameters and freshness, normalize results, and validate relationships without flattening meaningful states.
capabilities.tierRationale: Broad meaningful report coverage is a primary release outcome.

applicability.notes: The Reports API is a published QuickBooks Online Accounting API surface. Connected-company availability and population remain separate evidence states.

transactions: At least two relevant periods where comparisons apply

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Official endpoint review, fixture normalization tests, sandbox retrieval, cross-report assertions, and manual UI comparison.
limitations: A successful request is only availability evidence, not coverage.

capabilities.name: API rate, batch, and operation budgets
capabilities.purpose: Keep interactive reads and bounded operations inside documented limits while exposing throttling and stopping before unsafe volume.
capabilities.tierRationale: Every large historical or continual operation depends on measured, enforced realm-level budgets.

applicability.notes: Published sandbox and Production REST limits apply per realm/app, but the official batch pages currently disagree on payload guidance.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Resolve the official batch guidance conflict, add static budget tests, then run an explicitly approved sandbox benchmark below published ceilings.
limitations: The batch guide says up to 10 payloads while the current limits page recommends at most 30; use neither as an approved application budget until reconciled.
Published ceilings are not a target throughput profile.

capabilities.name: Full QBO data pagination
capabilities.purpose: Inspect every in-scope record rather than treating a 100-row response as a complete catalog.
capabilities.tierRationale: Coverage, drift, provenance, and governed management cannot be trusted from truncated entity sets.

applicability.notes: The official query language documents STARTPOSITION/MAXRESULTS, a default of 100, and a maximum of 1,000 entities per response.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Static query adapter tests plus an explicitly approved read-only pagination benchmark.
limitations: The current explorer uses a 100-row cap and does not prove completeness.

capabilities.name: Recurring transaction templates
capabilities.purpose: Represent the recurring-service line with scheduled, reminder, and unscheduled templates without confusing templates with generated transactions.
capabilities.tierRationale: Recurring templates broaden the continual-service story after the underlying invoice, sales-receipt, expense, and journal lifecycles are stable.

applicability.notes: The Canada product documents recurring templates for Advanced; the REST minor-version history documents read, create, and delete operations.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Official product and minor-version review, per-operation API Explorer review, then separately approved sandbox template fixtures.
limitations: Update support is not established by the reviewed release notes.
Generated occurrences require their own managed lifecycle and idempotency evidence.

capabilities.name: Multicurrency and exchange effects
capabilities.purpose: Represent foreign-currency customers, vendors, accounts, transactions, and exchange effects only when the company setting is intentionally enabled.
capabilities.tierRationale: Multicurrency materially expands support coverage but is irreversible and should not block the base-CAD business spine.

applicability.notes: The Canada product supports multicurrency for Advanced, but enabling it cannot be undone or change the home currency later.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Official Canada product review, read-only Preferences observation, accounting fixtures, and a separately approved sandbox-only activation decision.
limitations: Do not enable multicurrency in Production as a discovery action; the product setting is irreversible.
Existing entity currency assignments cannot simply be changed in place.

capabilities.name: Enhanced custom fields
capabilities.purpose: Represent approved support dimensions on sales forms, purchase forms, expenses, customers, and vendors without inventing generic ungoverned metadata.
capabilities.tierRationale: Enhanced custom fields are an Advanced breadth feature and report dimension after the business spine is coherent.

applicability.notes: Enhanced custom fields are documented for the Canada Advanced product. Premium API use depends on partner tier, restricted scope, and supported entity.

entitlements: Restricted Custom Fields scope for premium API use

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Official Canada product and premium API review, entitlement observation, then fixture coverage by supported entity.
limitations: The app's current partner tier and restricted scope are unobserved.
Field count and entity support must be read from current entitlement instead of hardcoded.

capabilities.name: Attachments and document links
capabilities.purpose: Exercise safe document attachment, relationship, metadata, retrieval, and retention boundaries for support cases.
capabilities.tierRationale: Attachments are significant support breadth but are not required to establish the accounting spine.

applicability.notes: The Accounting API documents the Attachable resource and published attachment limits.

capabilities.evidenceMethod: API Explorer and limits review, privacy-approved fixture files, mocked contract tests, then separately approved sandbox upload/download checks.
limitations: No private customer document may be used as a fixture.
Attachment retention and sensitive-content policy require approval before storage.

capabilities.name: Time activity and project labour
capabilities.purpose: Represent employee and contractor time against customers/projects so service delivery and project cost stories are believable.
capabilities.tierRationale: Time strengthens service/project coverage after customers, projects, items, and core transactions exist.

applicability.notes: TimeActivity is a documented Accounting API transaction; richer payroll compensation and Workforce surfaces require separate product and restricted-scope entitlement.

entitlements: Restricted payroll/time scopes only if later justified

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Accounting API entity review, product/entitlement review, deterministic time fixtures, and project-report assertions.
limitations: Payroll compensation is not part of the base Accounting scope.
The rebuild should default to safe time and summary coverage rather than payroll-detail generation.

capabilities.name: Payroll summary and clearing coverage
capabilities.purpose: Maintain believable payroll expense, liability, cash, and clearing effects without fabricating employee payroll detail or filings.
capabilities.tierRationale: A long-lived business needs explainable staff cost, but payroll detail has elevated privacy, entitlement, tax, and accounting risk.

applicability.notes: Payroll/Workforce availability depends on subscription. Restricted payroll compensation APIs do not authorize payroll generation for this app.

entitlements: Payroll subscription only if manually observed
transactions: Reviewed aggregate journal and payment evidence

capabilities.evidenceMethod: Manual product/entitlement inventory, accountant-reviewed aggregate fixtures, and redacted report/control-account evidence.
limitations: No personal payroll data, tax identifiers, compensation details, or filing automation enters the fixture set.
Any future payroll API use requires a separate privacy and authorization proposal.

reports.name: Balance Sheet
reports.businessQuestion: What does the company own, owe, and retain at the end of a period?

applicability.notes: The report is named in the current Reports API table. Connected-company availability and populated output remain separate evidence states.

assertions: Assets equal liabilities plus equity within the documented rounding tolerance.
Receivable and payable totals agree to related aging controls within documented scope.

reports.name: Profit and Loss
reports.businessQuestion: How much did the company earn and spend during a period?

applicability.notes: The report is named in the current Reports API table. Connected-company availability and populated output remain separate evidence states.

expectedNonZero: COGS when inventory is in scope
assertions: Net income equals income less cost of goods sold and expenses within tolerance.
Period results align with the blueprint's cadence and seasonality bands.

reports.name: Trial Balance
reports.businessQuestion: Do account debit and credit balances form a complete balanced ledger at a point in time?

applicability.notes: The current Reports API table names Trial Balance. The catalog uses the URL-safe TrialBalance endpoint spelling pending a non-mutating connected-company check.

assertions: Total debits equal total credits within tolerance.

reports.name: General Ledger
reports.businessQuestion: Which posting transactions explain each account balance during a period?

applicability.notes: The current Reports API table names General Ledger Detail. Connected-company availability and populated output remain separate evidence states.

assertions: Opening balance plus period activity equals closing balance for selected control accounts.

reports.name: Statement of Cash Flows
reports.businessQuestion: How did operating, investing, and financing activity change cash during the period?

applicability.notes: The report is named in the current Reports API table. Connected-company availability and populated output remain separate evidence states.

assertions: Opening cash plus net change equals closing cash within tolerance.

reports.name: Accounts Receivable Aging
reports.businessQuestion: Which customers owe money and how overdue are their balances?

applicability.notes: A/R Aging Summary is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Total aging agrees to the receivable control balance within scope and tolerance.

reports.name: Accounts Payable Aging
reports.businessQuestion: Which vendors are owed money and how overdue are the balances?

applicability.notes: A/P Aging Summary is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Total aging agrees to the payable control balance within scope and tolerance.

reports.name: Profit and Loss Detail
reports.businessQuestion: Which transactions explain each income and expense total for the period?

applicability.notes: Profit and Loss Detail is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Detail rows roll to the Profit and Loss totals for the same parameters within tolerance.

reports.name: Customer Balance Summary
reports.businessQuestion: Which customers hold receivable balances at the report date?

applicability.notes: Customer Balance Summary is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Customer balances total to the same scoped receivable amount as the aging summary within tolerance.

reports.name: Customer Balance Detail
reports.businessQuestion: Which transactions explain each customer's receivable balance?

applicability.notes: Customer Balance Detail is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Detail movements explain the Customer Balance Summary for the same scope and date.

reports.name: A/R Aging Detail
reports.businessQuestion: Which open receivable transactions make up each aging bucket?

applicability.notes: A/R Aging Detail is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Detail rows roll to A/R Aging Summary buckets and total within tolerance.

reports.name: Vendor Balance Summary
reports.businessQuestion: Which vendors hold payable balances at the report date?

applicability.notes: Vendor Balance Summary is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Vendor balances total to the same scoped payable amount as the aging summary within tolerance.

reports.name: Vendor Balance Detail
reports.businessQuestion: Which transactions explain each vendor's payable balance?

applicability.notes: Vendor Balance Detail is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Detail movements explain the Vendor Balance Summary for the same scope and date.

reports.name: A/P Aging Detail
reports.businessQuestion: Which open payable transactions make up each aging bucket?

applicability.notes: A/P Aging Detail is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Detail rows roll to A/P Aging Summary buckets and total within tolerance.

reports.name: Expenses by Vendor Summary
reports.businessQuestion: Which vendors account for operating spend during the period?

applicability.notes: Expenses by Vendor is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Vendor expense totals roll to the corresponding scoped expense total within tolerance.

reports.name: Sales by Department Summary
reports.businessQuestion: How do sales differ across enabled locations or departments?

applicability.notes: Sales by Department is named in the current Reports API table and requires department/location tracking plus populated data.

assertions: Department totals and unassigned amounts reconcile to the applicable scoped sales total.

reports.name: Account List
reports.businessQuestion: Does the company have the intended active and inactive account structure?

applicability.notes: Account List is named in the current Reports API table.

assertions: Required blueprint accounts exist exactly once and unexpected accounts are classified for review.

reports.name: Sales by Customer Summary
reports.businessQuestion: Which customer segments produce revenue during the period?

applicability.notes: The report is named in the current Reports API table. Connected-company population remains separate evidence.

assertions: Customer totals roll to the applicable sales total within documented scope.

reports.name: Income by Customer Summary
reports.businessQuestion: How is income distributed across customers and project-oriented work?

applicability.notes: The report is named in the current Reports API table. Project interpretation and connected-company population remain separate evidence.

assertions: Customer income totals agree to the corresponding scoped income total within tolerance.

reports.name: Sales by Product/Service Summary
reports.businessQuestion: Which products and services generate sales?

applicability.notes: The report is named in the current Reports API table. Connected-company population remains separate evidence.

assertions: Item sales totals roll to the applicable sales total within documented scope.

reports.name: Sales by Class Summary
reports.businessQuestion: How do sales differ across approved operating classes?

applicability.notes: Endpoint is documented and requires class tracking plus populated class data.

assertions: Class totals and unclassified amounts reconcile to the applicable scoped sales total.

reports.name: Inventory Valuation Summary
reports.businessQuestion: What inventory quantity and value does the company hold at a point in time?

applicability.notes: Endpoint is documented and requires inventory support plus populated inventory items.

assertions: Inventory total agrees to the scoped inventory asset control balance within tolerance.

reports.name: Inventory Valuation Detail
reports.businessQuestion: Which transactions explain inventory quantity and value changes?

applicability.notes: Endpoint is documented and requires inventory support plus lifecycle transactions.

assertions: Detail movements roll to the summary for the same scope and date.

reports.name: Project Profitability
reports.businessQuestion: Which projects are profitable after related income, costs, and time?

applicability.notes: Projects are documented for Advanced. Project Profitability is a product report candidate but is not named in the current Reports API endpoint table.

assertions: Project income less project costs equals project profit within tolerance.
reports.uiNavigation: QBO Reports > search for Project Profitability; exact label and availability require a manual connected-company observation.

reports.name: Sales Tax Liability
reports.businessQuestion: What tax was collected, recoverable, adjusted, and payable for the filing period?

applicability.notes: The Canada product documents a Sales Tax Liability report and province-specific GST/HST/PST/QST detail. The Reports API TaxSummary endpoint is documented for France only.

expectedNonZero: Net liability where blueprint calls for it
assertions: Report amounts reconcile to scoped tax control accounts and managed taxable lifecycles within tolerance.
reports.uiNavigation: QBO Reports > Standard reports > search Sales Tax Liability; use the Sales Tax centre for return preparation and payment evidence.
knownDiscrepancies: The published Reports API TaxSummary row is France-only and cannot be treated as a Canadian Sales Tax Liability endpoint.

reports.name: Budget vs Actual
reports.businessQuestion: How does actual performance compare with the approved plan?

applicability.notes: The Canada product supports budgets and budget comparisons; Budget vs Actual is not named in the current Reports API endpoint table.

assertions: Actual totals agree to the corresponding financial report scope.
reports.uiNavigation: QBO Reports > Financial planning > Budgets, then open the budget comparison view.

reports.name: Reconciliation Summary and Evidence
reports.businessQuestion: Does the recorded account balance agree with the approved statement and outstanding items?

applicability.notes: The Canada product automatically creates a static report for each completed reconciliation; it is not named in the current Reports API endpoint table.

assertions: Statement balance plus or minus documented outstanding items agrees to the scoped book balance.
Evidence state never claims official QBO completion from inference alone.
reports.uiNavigation: QBO Settings > Reconcile > History by account, or Reports > search Reconciliation Reports.
knownDiscrepancies: The reconciliation report is a static snapshot; later transaction changes can make it differ from live account reports.

reports.name: Journal
